signals.title: Cursor Cloud Agents can be Running before executable readiness when account-level MCP discovery stalls
signals.title_zh: Cursor Cloud Agents 在 Account-level MCP Discovery 阻塞时会出现 Running 但尚未达到可执行就绪
signals.summary: A reproducible Cursor Cloud Agents failure reached environment/API Running while the first model call never left the service. Cursor staff traced the affected runs to newly enabled account-level HTTP MCP servers; disabling the two offending servers restored first-token output, isolating the failure to MCP discovery/auth before model execution.
signals.summary_zh: 一组可复现的 Cursor Cloud Agents 故障显示：Environment/API 已进入 Running，但首个 Model Call 从未离开服务端。Cursor 员工把受影响运行追溯到新启用的 Account-level HTTP MCP Server；禁用两个问题 Server 后 First-token Output 恢复，从而把故障定位到 Model Execution 之前的 MCP Discovery/Auth。

researchValue.failure: A runtime can report Running after environment creation even though dependency discovery prevents the worker from becoming executable and no model/tool work can start.
researchValue.finding: Disabling the two newly added account-level MCP servers restored first-token output across fresh runs while other connected services remained enabled.
researchValue.mechanism: Separate environment/process Running from executable readiness, make MCP discovery/auth a terminating dependency-admission state, and surface the exact failing dependency before declaring active work.
researchValue.implication: Digital-employee dashboards should distinguish slot/process state from worker-ready state and treat tool discovery as an observable admission gate with timeout and fault attribution.

signals.title: GitHub moves content exclusions into the shared context boundary for Copilot app and CLI agentic workflows
signals.title_zh: GitHub 将 Content Exclusion 下沉到 Copilot App 与 CLI Agentic Workflow 的共享 Context Boundary
signals.summary: GitHub Copilot app and CLI now honor enterprise, organization, and repository content-exclusion policies so excluded files are not used as context across agentic workflows.
signals.summary_zh: GitHub Copilot App 与 CLI 现在遵循 Enterprise、Organization 与 Repository 配置的 Content Exclusion Policy，使被排除文件不会进入 Agentic Workflow 的上下文。

researchValue.failure: A sensitive path can remain protected in one UI while leaking into another agentic surface if exclusion is implemented per client rather than at context admission.
researchValue.mechanism: Apply administrator-defined content exclusions when constructing agent context across app and CLI surfaces instead of treating exclusions as a presentation-layer feature.
researchValue.implication: Governed digital employees should enforce content-access policy at the shared harness/context boundary so every execution surface consumes the same admissible evidence set.

signals.title: Codex re-admits managed worktree forks against destination trust, configuration, and session state
signals.title_zh: Codex 在 Managed Worktree Fork 时按目标 Trust、Configuration 与 Session State 重新准入
signals.summary: Codex added managed worktree creation for new and forked conversations. It loads destination configuration, binds the replacement thread to the checkout, inherits history only for forks, rejects explicitly untrusted sources, requires an idle primary session without queued input, and refuses forks when developer instructions differ.
signals.summary_zh: Codex 新增 Managed Worktree，可为新会话或 Fork 会话创建受管 Checkout。它读取目标 Configuration、把 Replacement Thread 绑定到目标 Checkout，仅在 Fork 时继承 History；同时拒绝显式 Untrusted Source，要求 Primary Session Idle 且无 Queued Input，并在 Developer Instructions 不一致时拒绝 Fork。

researchValue.failure: Forking conversation history into a checkout with different developer instructions, untrusted provenance, or active queued work can transfer context and authority into an incompatible execution environment.
researchValue.mechanism: Re-evaluate source trust and destination configuration before fork, require an idle source session, bind the new thread to the destination checkout, and inherit history only when destination policy remains compatible.
researchValue.implication: Workspace/session transitions in long-running agents should be treated as re-admission points rather than transparent filesystem operations.

signals.title: OpenAI Agents SDK gives the agent graph a stable identity shared by RunState, tool tracking, and sandbox resume
signals.title_zh: OpenAI Agents SDK 为 Agent Graph 建立由 RunState、Tool Tracking 与 Sandbox Resume 共享的稳定身份
signals.summary: OpenAI Agents SDK extracted deterministic agent-graph identity shared by RunState, tool tracking, and sandbox resume. The graph traverses handoffs and agent-as-tool instances so nested approvals can be restored and differentiates otherwise colliding agent identities with normalized tool/capability signatures.
signals.summary_zh: OpenAI Agents SDK 抽离出由 RunState、Tool Tracking 与 Sandbox Resume 共享的确定性 Agent Graph Identity。该图遍历 Handoff 与 Agent-as-tool 实例，使 Nested Approval 可在恢复时重新绑定，并通过规范化 Tool/Capability Signature 区分潜在冲突的 Agent Identity。

researchValue.failure: After serialization or resume, nested approvals and sandbox/tool state can bind to transient object identity or an ambiguous same-name agent rather than the original execution principal.
researchValue.mechanism: Derive deterministic identities from the reachable agent graph, including handoffs, agent-as-tool relationships, and normalized tool/capability signatures, and reuse those identities across persisted runtime subsystems.
researchValue.implication: Durable multi-agent runtimes need a stable principal graph separate from in-process object identity so recovered authority and tool state attach to the correct agent.

signals.title: MCP Python SDK binds bearer-token authority to the exact resource server
signals.title_zh: MCP Python SDK 将 Bearer Token 权限绑定到确切 Resource Server
signals.summary: MCP Python SDK added AuthSettings.validate_token_resource so a resource server can reject a bearer token whose AccessToken.resource does not match the exact resource_server_url. The migration path warns when resource validation is not configured and plans to make validation the default for resource servers in 3.0.
signals.summary_zh: MCP Python SDK 新增 AuthSettings.validate_token_resource，使 Resource Server 可拒绝 AccessToken.resource 与确切 resource_server_url 不匹配的 Bearer Token。迁移路径会在未配置 Resource Validation 时警告，并计划在 3.0 对 Resource Server 默认启用验证。

researchValue.failure: A token can be validly signed and carry sufficient scopes yet still be intended for another resource, creating a confused-deputy authorization path if the target audience is not checked.
researchValue.mechanism: Bind accepted bearer tokens to the current MCP endpoint by validating AccessToken.resource against the exact resource_server_url, or require the verifier to enforce an equivalent audience binding.
researchValue.implication: Tool capability and token possession are insufficient; MCP call-time authorization should include the concrete target resource in the authority check.

signals.title: Failure-risk prediction is useful for escalation, but does not identify which collaboration protocol pays off
signals.title_zh: 失败风险预测可用于 Escalation，但不足以判断哪种 Collaboration Protocol 值得付出成本
signals.summary: A controlled study runs each problem under four collaboration protocols while holding the solver fixed. A post-answer failure probe predicts baseline failure strongly, but its ability to predict value from specific planner-executor-reviewer or broadcast protocols is much weaker; conservative routers under-escalate and higher-solve routers often over-escalate.
signals.summary_zh: 一项受控研究在固定 Solver 的情况下让每个问题分别运行四种 Collaboration Protocol。Post-answer Failure Probe 对 Baseline Failure 的预测很强，但对特定 Planner-Executor-Reviewer 或 Broadcast Protocol 是否有价值的预测明显较弱；保守 Router 容易 Under-escalate，而高 Solve Router 又常 Over-escalate。

researchValue.failure: A single confidence or failure-risk gate can decide that more collaboration is needed while still choosing the wrong collaboration structure or spending substantially more tokens than its benefit justifies.
researchValue.finding: On 4,181 competition-level math problems, the post-answer probe ranked baseline failures at 0.8847 AUROC, but protocol-specific value prediction for PER and Broadcast was much weaker at 0.1674 and 0.1041 AUPRC; protocol profiles also varied by task.
researchValue.mechanism: Separate failure-risk admission from protocol-specific routing and evaluate candidate protocols under paired tasks with explicit solve and token-cost accounting.
researchValue.implication: Digital-employee escalation should not be a binary 'add more agents' switch; admission, collaboration topology, and cost budget should be independently governed.

signals.title: Supply-network resilience is phase-specific and emerges from trust-mediated agent coordination
signals.title_zh: 供应网络韧性具有阶段性，并由 Trust-mediated Agent Coordination 共同塑造
signals.summary: An open-access agent-based supply-chain study models load redistribution under trust and capacity constraints and evaluates absorptive, adaptive, containment, and recovery phases separately. It finds heterogeneous temporal outcomes across heuristic, supervised-imitation, online-adaptive, and cross-entropy policies and across network structures.
signals.summary_zh: 一项开放获取的 Agent-based Supply-chain 研究在 Trust 与 Capacity Constraint 下建模 Load Redistribution，并分别评估 Absorptive、Adaptive、Containment 与 Recovery 阶段。研究显示，不同 Heuristic、Supervised Imitation、Online Adaptive、Cross-entropy Policy 以及不同 Network Structure 会形成异质的时序结果。

researchValue.failure: Static topology or eventual recovery metrics can hide whether a multi-agent organization absorbs a shock, adapts, contains cascades, and recovers at the right times.
researchValue.finding: The study reports phase-specific differences in absorptive, adaptive, and recovery behavior as trust-mediated decision policies and network structures vary.
researchValue.mechanism: Represent disruption response as policy-driven load redistribution among capacity-constrained agents with trust-dependent local decisions, then evaluate resilience by phase rather than by one terminal metric.
researchValue.implication: Operational digital-employee teams may need phase-specific resilience and trust metrics instead of treating eventual completion as sufficient evidence of healthy recovery.
